# AcceptLanguage

Source: https://accept-language.hexdocs.pm/AcceptLanguage.md

# `AcceptLanguage`
[🔗](https://github.com/cyril/accept_language.ex/blob/main/lib/accept_language.ex#L3)

A lightweight, zero-dependency Elixir library for parsing the `Accept-Language`
HTTP header field as defined in RFC 7231 Section 5.3.5, with full support for
BCP 47 language tags.

## Purpose

The `Accept-Language` request header field is sent by user agents to indicate
the set of natural languages preferred in the response. This library parses
that header and matches the user's language preferences against your
application's available languages, respecting quality values, wildcards,
exclusions, and the Basic Filtering matching scheme defined in RFC 4647.

## Standards compliance

This implementation conforms to:

  * [RFC 7231 Section 5.3.5](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7231#section-5.3.5) —
    Accept-Language header field definition
  * [RFC 7231 Section 5.3.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7231#section-5.3.1) —
    Quality values (qvalues) syntax
  * [RFC 4647 Section 2.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4647#section-2.1) —
    Basic Language Range syntax
  * [RFC 4647 Section 3.3.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4647#section-3.3.1) —
    Basic Filtering matching scheme
  * [BCP 47](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp47) —
    Tags for Identifying Languages

> RFC 7231 obsoletes RFC 2616 (the original HTTP/1.1 specification).
> The `Accept-Language` header behavior remains unchanged, ensuring full
> backward compatibility.

## Usage

    AcceptLanguage.negotiate("da, en-GB;q=0.8, en;q=0.7", [:en, :da])
    # => :da

## Quality values

Quality values (q-values) indicate relative preference, ranging from `0`
(not acceptable) to `1` (most preferred). When omitted, the default is `1`.

    AcceptLanguage.negotiate("da, en-GB;q=0.8, en;q=0.7", [:en, :da])
    # => :da  (q=1 beats q=0.8)

    AcceptLanguage.negotiate("da, en-GB;q=0.8, en;q=0.7", [:en, :"en-GB"])
    # => :"en-GB"  (q=0.8 beats q=0.7)

## Basic Filtering

A language range matches a language tag if it exactly equals the tag, or if
it exactly equals a prefix of the tag such that the first character following
the prefix is `-`:

    AcceptLanguage.negotiate("zh", [:"zh-TW"])
    # => :"zh-TW"

    AcceptLanguage.negotiate("zh", [:zhx])
    # => nil  (different language code, no hyphen boundary)

## Wildcards and exclusions

    # Wildcard matches any unmatched language
    AcceptLanguage.negotiate("de, *;q=0.5", [:ja])
    # => :ja

    # q=0 excludes a language
    AcceptLanguage.negotiate("*, en;q=0", [:en, :fr])
    # => :fr

## Concurrency safety

This function is pure: it takes immutable inputs and returns an immutable
value, with no side effects. It is safe to call concurrently from any
number of processes without coordination.

# `negotiate`

```elixir
@spec negotiate(String.t() | nil, [atom()]) :: atom() | nil
```

Negotiates the best language match from an `Accept-Language` header value
and a list of available languages.

Parses the header, validates and ranks language preferences, then applies
the Basic Filtering matching scheme defined in RFC 4647 Section 3.3.1
to find the optimal match.

## Matching criteria (in priority order)

  1. **Quality values** — Higher q-values indicate stronger preference
  2. **Declaration order** — When q-values are equal, earlier declaration wins
  3. **Prefix matching** — `en` matches `en-US`, `en-GB`, etc.
  4. **Wildcards** — `*` matches any language not explicitly listed
  5. **Exclusions** — `q=0` explicitly excludes a language

Invalid language ranges or malformed quality values in the header are
silently ignored, allowing the function to handle real-world headers
that may not strictly conform to specifications.

The returned atom preserves the exact form passed in `available_langtags`.

## Parameters

  * `field` — The `Accept-Language` header value as a string, or `nil`
    when the header is absent. Typically obtained via
    `Plug.Conn.get_req_header(conn, "accept-language")`.
  * `available_langtags` — List of atoms representing the languages your
    application supports

## Complexity

Time: O(n log n + p × a) where n = number of language entries,
p = preferred count, a = available count.
Space: O(n + a) for intermediate lists.

## Examples

    iex> AcceptLanguage.negotiate("da, en-GB;q=0.8, en;q=0.7", [:en, :da])
    :da

    iex> AcceptLanguage.negotiate("*, en;q=0", [:en, :fr])
    :fr

    iex> AcceptLanguage.negotiate("ja, zh", [:en, :fr])
    nil

    iex> AcceptLanguage.negotiate(nil, [:en, :fr])
    nil
